JevBench v1.2.4: a service on another entrant's model is listed, not ranked

classifier.dev (fast tier) was #1 with 84.8. It is not its own model. Its own
pages say so — "The fast tier is Jev, TypeSafe's decision model"
(classifier.dev/benchmark, read 20 Sep 2026) — and its API answers with
"model": "jev-1.13.0", the same version this benchmark measures directly as
Jev 1.13.0. Ranking it put the same model in the list twice: once at TypeSafe's
per-token tariff, once at classifier.dev's flat plan.

So from v1.2.4 there is a general rule, not a one-off: a service that runs
another entrant's model is listed with all of its scores and axes, but is not
ranked against the models. classifier.dev keeps every number, axis, cost basis,
radar and per-task outcome and loses only its rank; Jev 1.13.0 is #1 and every
other row moves up one place. No measurement, no axis and no score changed.

What it adds, in its own words, is the price and — on the smart tier, which we
never ran — an orchestration layer: "The smart tier is Jev plus a reasoning
model re-asking only the answers Jev put under 0.7 confidence." That is
escalation on low confidence, a model cascade; not best-of-N, not
self-consistency, not a committee. Their published escalation model is
gemini-3.8-flash.

The honorable-mention note keeps the price caveat ($0.0033 per 1,000 decisions
assumes the $20/month Pro plan at full use, 200,000/day; at a tenth of that it
is $0.033) and states honestly that their pages do not say how the flat rate is
funded, so we do not know their cost basis. It also reports the one place the
fast tier measurably differs from Jev on our set: 97.3 % vs 94.5 % on judge
items, 70.5 % vs 74.1 % on hard ones.

Artifact: every row now carries "listing" (ranked / honorable_mention /
partial); only a ranked row carries a rank. tests/test_honorable_mentions.py

JevBench v1.2.3: cost correction — each decision counted once, and priced once

A reader read our Cost column as dollars per 1,000 tokens and said Jev is 4.2 cents per
million, not per thousand. He is right about the tariff and we always used it: Jev 1.13.0
is $0.042 per MILLION input tokens, output free (docs.typesafe.ai/models). Our column is
dollars per 1,000 DECISIONS, and one decision is a whole question — 950 input tokens on
average for Jev. Checking that claim turned up three real arithmetic mistakes of our own:

1. The v1.1 and v1.1.3 cost averages used a row list that held the 242-decision
   standard+judge run twice and the 72 easy decisions once — 556 rows instead of 314.
2. Rows priced from the gemini-3.1-flash-lite token counts used that run's
   standard+judge-only average (452 input tokens per decision) for all 314 v1.1
   decisions, instead of its average over all 314 (383).
3. Requests whose answer came back unparseable were left unpriced although the provider
   billed them (HTTP 200, tokens generated). Only DeepSeek V4.1 Flash had any: 9 of 314.

No tariff was wrong, no measurement, item or answer changed, and no rank changed.
Fifteen rows get 1.5-11 % cheaper (JevBench Score up by at most 0.2 points); DeepSeek
V4.1 Flash gets 2.6 % more expensive (58.1 -> 57.8).

The unit is now spelled out wherever the number appears — table header, chart labels,
chart footers, axis title, README, RESULTS-v1.2.md and the artifact's cost_unit block —
with the worked example that makes it unmistakable.

Corrected prices and their derivation: results/v1.2/cost-correction-v1.2.3.json, applied
by scripts/v1.2/finalize.py. Nine new tests in tests/test_cost_correction.py check that
every price is its tariff times its tokens over exactly 314 + 220 decisions, so neither
mistake can come back. 54 tests pass; both leak checks clean.
